issue.title: The configure script doesn't allow running ASan with PyMalloc

labels.name: type-bug
labels.description: An unexpected behavior, bug, or error

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

The `--with-address-sanitizer` configure option overrides whatever pymalloc option one provides which it should not.

We should either allow it to work with `--with-pymalloc`, or, delete the line that disables pymalloc. I discussed it a bit during EP2025 sprint with @encukou .

This is done due to the line here:
https://github.com/python/cpython/blame/4a151cae3317ce133bdf0792fb1064c5030e588c/configure#L13352

I believe that CPython works fine with ASan + PyMalloc. I have tested it by removing the line above. Then the `import _testcapi; _testcapi.WITH_PYMALLOC` is `True` and there doesn't seem to be ASan crashes. However, there are leaks being detected, even when building Python, so I did all this with `export ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0`.

It is also worth noting that we:
1. List the `--without-pymalloc` flag in the  [devguide](https://github.com/python/devguide/blob/2fad8516e646a9ceedd32566587f7200b1610649/development-tools/clang.rst#:~:text=The%20%2D%2Dwithout%2Dpymalloc%20option%20is%20not%20necessary%20(tests%20should%20pass%20without%20it)%2C%20but%20disabling%20pymalloc%20helps%20ASan%20uncover%20more%20bugs%20(ASan%20does%20not%20track%20individual%20allocations%20done%20by%20pymalloc).) when showing how to run ASan.
2. We mention there, that the flag is not necessary, but it makes ASan more effective.
3. We mention in CPython docs that it makes sense to disable PyMalloc when running ASan [here](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/c-api/memory.rst#:~:text=Typically%2C%20it%20makes%20sense%20to%20disable%20the%20pymalloc%20allocator%20when%20building%20Python%20with%20AddressSanitizer%20(%3Aoption%3A%60%2D%2Dwith%2Daddress%2Dsanitizer%60)%20which%20helps%20uncover%20low%20level%20bugs%20within%20the%20C%20code.)

 

### CPython versions tested on:

CPython main branch

### Operating systems tested on:

_No response_

comments.body:
> We mention in CPython docs that it makes sense to disable PyMalloc when running ASan [here](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/c-api/memory.rst#:~:text=Typically%2C%20it%20makes%20sense%20to%20disable%20the%20pymalloc%20allocator%20when%20building%20Python%20with%20AddressSanitizer%20(%3Aoption%3A%60%2D%2Dwith%2Daddress%2Dsanitizer%60)%20which%20helps%20uncover%20low%20level%20bugs%20within%20the%20C%20code.)

To be clear: we added that line recently. I trusted the devguide & didn't check the configure script.

Disabling pymalloc by default in ASan/MSan builds makes sense, but, `--with-pymalloc` should override the default.
